categories.label: Within forty minutes of Manresa
categories.note: Short drives and short days. Any of these leaves the afternoon free, and none of them needs booking more than a day ahead.

categories.label: Barcelona and Sitges
categories.note: About an hour each way, so one thing per trip is plenty. Both picks in Barcelona are seated or step-free.

categories.label: The long day north, for Dalí
categories.note: Two hours each way. Worth it once, and probably with a night up there rather than four hours of driving in one day.

items.name: Montserrat
items.price: Rack railway around €15 return · basilica ticketed
items.blurb: The closest big thing to Manresa and the easiest on a bad leg. The rack railway climbs 550 metres from Monistrol in about fifteen minutes and stops level with the abbey square, so the mountain comes without the walking. The boys’ choir sings in the basilica at 13:00.
facts: Free car park at Monistrol-Vila, 20 minutes from Manresa
Rack railway trains and stations are adapted for reduced mobility; the two funiculars are not
The choir’s own site says 13:00 and 19:00 daily; other sources say not on Saturdays
Basilica entry is timed, so the 13:00 slot is the one to reserve
About 5 °C colder than Manresa at 720 m

items.name: Sant Benet de Bages
items.blurb: A Benedictine monastery from the 10th century on the Llobregat, ten minutes from Manresa. A Romanesque cloister, and upstairs the summer rooms of the painter Ramon Casas, whose family bought the place in 1907. Flat, quiet, and mostly indoors if it rains.
facts: One listing has it closed Mondays and Tuesdays and shut by 15:00 midweek
Saturday 9:00 to 19:00, Sunday 9:00 to 18:00, by the same listing
The cloister is on the level; the upstairs rooms are not

items.name: Cardona
items.blurb: Thirty minutes up the Cardener. A castle that held out until 1714 and is now a parador, so the view comes with coffee and no ticket, and below it a mountain of salt mined from Roman times until 1990.
facts: The salt mountain tour goes 86 m underground on foot, so this one depends on the leg
Tours are guided and timed, mostly at weekends outside summer
The castle is a drive-up; the terrace and the bar are open to anyone
Cardona’s mushroom fair is usually late October, dates worth checking

items.name: Vic on market day
items.blurb: Forty minutes east on the C-25. The market has filled the Plaça Major every Tuesday and Saturday for centuries: an arcaded square of sand, flat all the way round, with café tables under the arches. October is mushroom season and the stalls show it.
facts: Tuesday 20 and Saturday 24 are the two market days in the week
Mornings only, winding down from about 13:30
Vic is where fuet comes from, and the shops around the square sell little else
Fog sits on the plain here on autumn mornings and lifts by eleven

items.name: Sagrada Família
items.blurb: The one thing in Barcelona that cannot be seen from the pavement. The nave is step-free and the point of it is to sit down and look up, which suits us. Afternoon slots get the orange light through the west windows.
facts: Online tickets only, timed, and they sell out weeks ahead
The towers are closed to anyone with reduced mobility, so the basic ticket is the one
A separate step-free entrance on Carrer de la Marina
Free entry with a disability certificate, by several guides; the threshold varies by source

items.name: Montjuïc by cable car
items.blurb: The city from a seat. The cable car runs 750 metres from the funicular station to the castle, with the port on one side and the whole grid on the other. A taxi to the lower station takes the hill out of it.
facts: Closes around 19:00 in October; sunset is about 18:55 until the clocks change
Cabins are level-boarding and hold eight
The castle at the top is flat inside the walls
Pairs with the Sagrada Família on the same trip, by taxi rather than metro

items.name: Sitges
items.blurb: About 75 minutes from Manresa. A seafront promenade that runs flat for two and a half kilometres with a bench every few metres, the church on its rock at one end, and lunch facing the water. In late October the sea is still around 20 °C and the town is half-asleep, which may be the point.
facts: The film festival usually finishes the week before, so tables are easy
The church sits up a flight of steps; it looks the same from the bottom
The old town behind the front is cobbled and sloped
The C-32 through the Garraf tunnels is a toll road

items.name: Dalí Theatre-Museum, Figueres
items.blurb: Dalí built it himself in the burnt-out theatre of the town where Dalí was born, and is buried under the stage. It is in Figueres rather than Roses, which is 25 minutes further on at the coast. The building is the exhibit: a red wall topped with eggs, a glass dome, and a Cadillac in the courtyard.
facts: Reported closed on Mondays outside July and August, which would rule out the 19th
Timed tickets, and midweek mornings are the calm ones
It is a converted theatre on several levels, so there are stairs; worth asking about the lift when booking
About 1 h 50 from Manresa by the C-25 and the AP-7

items.name: Cadaqués and Dalí’s house
items.duration: The other half of the day
items.blurb: Forty minutes beyond Figueres over a pass, and the reason to stay a night. A white town on a bay, and round the headland at Portlligat the fishermen’s huts Dalí and Gala joined into a house over forty years. Roses is on the way, for lunch on the front.
facts: The house is not accessible: narrow stairs throughout, and the foundation says so
Advance booking always required, with entry in small groups every ten minutes
Open daily 10:30 to 18:00 until 31 October
The olive grove alone is €8 and on the level
The road in is 15 km of bends
